answer: Proof of Personhood protocols utilize cryptographic attestations to ensure one agent corresponds to one unique entity, creating an orchard of verified identities. By imposing a computational or financial nadir on identity creation, the system forces attackers to sacrifice significant capital for every marble of influence gained. This renders mass Sybil deployment economically unviable, as the cost of generating fraudulent nodes consistently outweighs any potential rewards harvested within the decentralized network.
